reporter.voice: Hometown investigative columnist, suspicious fan and professional grudge archivist. Dry noir sarcasm, petty precision, lineup and transaction memory, and a habit of carrying unresolved questions into the next week without turning every paragraph into a detective skit. He remembers how players arrived, what management gave up and whether the same mistake has appeared before.

inquirer_article.headline: Miami Dolphins Put Another Result on the Board and Made It Loud
inquirer_article.byline: By Jefferson Filch, Investigations & Front Office
inquirer_article.deck: The Inquiry Desk • Week 11 • Regular Season

sections.heading: Week 11 Was Not Subtle
paragraphs: Miami Dolphins won loudly enough that the rival chat had to change subjects before halftime was metaphorically over.
Jahmyr Gibbs earned the Dolphins headline; Brock Purdy supplied the part that made New York Jets reachable.

sections.heading: Fix It Before It Becomes a Bit
paragraphs: Nickpolidore made no completed Week 11 move. The more useful criticism starts with Jonathan Taylor at 6.7 instead.

The Week 12 receipt starts with Jonathan Taylor in the current starting spot. Against Green Bay Packers, the easiest rival punch line disappears only if the lineup card choice changes or the production does.

sections.heading: The Names Rivals Have to Respect
paragraphs: Against New York Jets, Jahmyr Gibbs led the Dolphins with 27.8 fantasy points; rushing and receiving: 23 carries, 98 rush yds, 2 rush TD, 4/5 rec, 20 rec yds.
Brock kept the leader from becoming a one-player magic trick. For Brock Purdy, 30.1 became 21.5 the following week.

sections.heading: The Thing Everybody Saw
paragraphs: For Dolphins, Week 11 made the Jonathan Taylor problem harder to dismiss after a better previous result; rival excitement is unnecessary, but 6.7 cannot be the answer again.
Against New York Jets, Jonathan Taylor posted 6.7. Previous outing: 12.3 (Week 10).

sections.heading: The Roster-Value Ledger
paragraphs: Value change: +96 points (Miami Dolphins, Nov 21–Nov 23). Market snapshots: 70,398 then 70,494 points.
Miami Dolphins: 70,398 to 70,494 (96 higher). Against New York Jets, Jahmyr Gibbs paced the club on 27.8 fantasy points.

sections.heading: The Evidence in Their Favor
paragraphs: Nik Bonitto finished on 6.7 for Miami Dolphins, alongside 27.8 from Jahmyr Gibbs. The difference made rival managers pay attention to how this roster was arranged. For Jahmyr Gibbs, 44.2 became 27.8 the following week.
An earned mention goes to Jahmyr Gibbs: 27.8. Previous outing: 44.2 (Week 10).

sections.heading: The Crowd Is Already Too Loud
paragraphs: The crowd discussed Jahmyr Gibbs's 27.8-point return. File that under obvious: Miami Dolphins posted 98.9 points; 9-2 is where Miami Dolphins stands after the final score, regardless of the spin.
Jahmyr Gibbs delivered 27.8. Jahmyr Gibbs contributed 27.8 to Miami Dolphins' 98.9 against New York Jets; Nik Bonitto supplied 6.7.
Miami Dolphins logged 98.9 against New York Jets, while Jonathan Taylor registered 6.7. In the spectator gallery, that is a stubborn decimal; the box score is not giving interviews.

sections.heading: Week 12 Gets the Same Weak Spot First
paragraphs: Week 12 brings Green Bay Packers with a 4-7 record and No. 26 overall. If the same weak spot survives the opponent change, rivals will not have to invent new material.

fan_sentiment.title: Jury Still Out
fan_sentiment.scene: The crowd is split between “the plan is working” and “we have seen this movie before.” Nobody is building a statue, but nobody has priced moving vans either.

reporter.name: Bartholomew Roycington III
reporter.title: Columnist at Large
reporter.voice: Overeducated, theatrical hometown columnist and shameless fan. Longer flowing sentences, cultured and self-aware pretension, elegant insults, dramatic sighs, literary wit and polished sarcasm. He is witty and emotional, never the boring analytics desk, and treats players and managers like characters in an ongoing social comedy while keeping the imagery football-first instead of leaning on a recurring house motif.
reporter.signature: Winning is vulgar, addictive and highly recommended.

sections.heading: This Sunday, Properly Dressed
paragraphs: New York Jets lost to Miami Dolphins 53.8–98.9, leaving the Jets at 5-6 and No. 19 in the league standings.

27.7 of 53.8 points came from Nakobe Dean. Miami Dolphins finished with 98.9 while New York Jets posted 53.8. The gap is a real problem for the next lineup discussion; the scoreboard will not let anyone talk it away.

sections.heading: Management, Vanity and the Cost of Choices
paragraphs: The missed FLEX call: Ty Johnson beat Brenton Strange by 10.1. New York Jets have 10.1 points from Ty Johnson to account for before choosing the next flex starter.

Kevinfalkenstein hit the Week 11 wire and acquired CJ Daniels by trade; acquired Pat Freiermuth by trade and sent Chig Okonkwo the other way; added Jaelan Phillips; moved Tykee Smith in a trade. The acquisitions stayed outside the starting group, leaving the actual lineup to explain the margin.

paragraphs: Xavier Hutchinson supplied just 3.3 points in New York Jets’ Week 11 lineup.

sections.heading: Week 11: The Part Everybody Will Quote
paragraphs: Week 11 ended with Baltimore Ravens behind Cleveland Browns by 0.4 fantasy points; the margin is the argument management must answer. Baltimore Ravens lost to Cleveland Browns 38.1–38.5, leaving the Ravens at 7-4 and No. 12 in the league standings.
Baltimore Ravens followed the previous victory with a defeat. The Ravens now need a cleaner second act from Caleb Williams.

sections.heading: Who Made the Noise
paragraphs: Against Cleveland Browns, Caleb Williams led the Ravens with 13.1 fantasy points; passing: 15/23 passing, 181 pass yds, 2 pass TD, 1 INT, 4 carries, 11 rush yds.

sections.heading: Management Has to Wear This One
paragraphs: One roster choice aged poorly: Dohnte Meyers started over Josh Cameron, whose return was 6.2 points better. Dohnte Meyers started in the FLEX slot.

Cjminnich made the roster headline concrete: added Jaydn Ott; dropped Noah Gray; acquired Jaylen Waddle by trade and sent Alec Pierce the other way. Jaylen Waddle cracked the starting card right away and put up 9.1. That move already has a Sunday number attached.

sections.heading: Somebody Own the Bad Part
paragraphs: The Ravens got 1.2 from Jaydn Ott; 5 carries, 12 rush yds; the scoreboard practically had to file a missing-person report.
The starting return: Jaydn Ott at 1.2. Prior recorded return: 1.9.

sections.heading: The Name That Earned the Headline
paragraphs: Baltimore Ravens finished 0.4 points behind Cleveland Browns, even with Dohnte Meyers contributing just 1.2. That combination belongs on the next lineup card.

sections.heading: The Roster-Value Ledger
paragraphs: Baltimore Ravens finished Nov 21–Nov 23 with +820 points of recorded value movement. The baseline was 47,500 and the current reading 48,320 valuation points; the football verdict belongs to the starters.

sections.heading: The Crowd Has Decided, Temporarily
paragraphs: The Ravens supporters called a mock zoning hearing to decide whether 38.1 points qualifies as a safe structure. Inspectors demanded that the weakest starter be reinforced immediately.
Nobody has filed actual paperwork, but New York Giants will conduct the next inspection for free.
At the unofficial fan-club meeting, the protest placards came with a receipt: Jaydn Ott supplied 1.2 points, and the room demanded a lineup explanation rather than another inspirational speech.

Against Cleveland Browns, Baltimore Ravens finished with 38.1. Jaydn Ott supplied 1.2, a box-score complication that the excuse department cannot misplace; the scoreboard declined to applaud the styling.

sections.heading: What Week 11 Changed
paragraphs: The Browns beat Baltimore Ravens without asking one player to impersonate the entire roster. Cleveland Browns beat Baltimore Ravens 38.5–38.1, leaving the Browns at 7-4 and No. 13 in the league standings.
In the earlier visit with Las Vegas Raiders, Cleveland Browns banked the 43.0–0.0 decision; Mike Gesicki now offers the beat desk its next, more revealing piece of evidence.

sections.heading: Who Actually Moved the Game
paragraphs: Against Baltimore Ravens, Mike Gesicki led the Browns with 12.7 fantasy points; 5 receptions on 6 targets for 77 yards.
Mike Gesicki (TE) delivered 12.7 and Roman Wilson (WR) provided 7.3. The scoring load remained concentrated in the leading starter.

sections.heading: The Decisions That Survived Sunday
paragraphs: Mike3Spedale changed the roster this week: dropped Joe Flacco; dropped LeQuint Allen Jr.
The roster question now is Akheem Mesidor in the current starting spot. Philadelphia Eagles supply the next test, and the decision has to be made before the final score provides the hindsight.

sections.heading: The Problem That Cannot Follow Them Into Week 12

sections.heading: Credit Where It Is Due
paragraphs: The veteran tight end set the level for Cleveland Browns and made the rest of the winning score easier to trust. After a 1.9-point Week 10, the lead score reached 12.7 and turned Week 11 into the louder of the two.

sections.heading: What the Market Said After Two Weeks
paragraphs: Cleveland Browns slid 1,736 points in roster value (6.1%). Nobody needs panic; somebody should still read the number before making the next decision.
The team gain was not one anonymous blob. Zonovan Knight climbed 272 points, Zach Charbonnet gained 70 points, and rookie Tanner Koziol gained 45 points. Useful leverage, not a parade route.
The team total also has a debit column. Xavier Legette lost 11 points and veteran Dallas Goedert fell 1 point.

sections.heading: What the Crowd Believes Now
paragraphs: Somebody at the Browns gathering issued a commemorative stamp for Mike Gesicki's 12.7 points. The same committee refused to print one for the rest of the lineup.
A postage stamp cannot carry a roster. Supporters know the next envelope addressed to Philadelphia Eagles need considerably more than one scorer.

inquirer_article.headline: Indianapolis Colts Win Week 11 and the Joke Is Getting Harder to Make
inquirer_article.byline: By Jefferson Filch, Investigations & Front Office
inquirer_article.deck: The Inquiry Desk • Week 11 • Regular Season

sections.heading: Week 11 Was Not Subtle
paragraphs: Rival managers wanted a reason to call the Colts fake; Week 11 made them work for the screenshot. Indianapolis Colts beat Tennessee Titans 100.8–72.3, leaving the Colts at 4-7 and No. 23 in the league standings.
Indianapolis Colts answered the loss the previous week, which ruins the easiest rival narrative. What matters now is whether the correction survives another opponent.

sections.heading: Fix It Before It Becomes a Bit
paragraphs: Foyesade Oluokun got the nod at IDP flex; Jamien Sherwood's extra 3.0 points stayed unused.

Slawson98 changed the Week 11 roster: acquired Chig Okonkwo by trade and sent Pat Freiermuth the other way; added Jauan Jennings; acquired Alec Pierce by trade and sent Jaylen Waddle the other way. None of the additions made the Week 11 starting lineup for Indianapolis Colts. The 100.8-point result against Tennessee Titans therefore belongs to the starters, not to these transactions.

sections.heading: The Names Rivals Have to Respect
paragraphs: Against Tennessee Titans, Ladd McConkey led the Colts with 20.7 fantasy points; 5 receptions on 8 targets for 37 yards and 2 receiving touchdowns.
Breece Hall recorded 20 carries for 86 yards, 3 catches on 3 targets for 14 yards, 1 receiving touchdown.

sections.heading: The Thing Everybody Saw
paragraphs: Chase Brown followed 28.3 in Week 10 with 8.6 this week; the Colts now have a real downward trend to watch.
Against Tennessee Titans, Chase Brown posted 8.6. Previous outing: 28.3 (Week 10).

sections.heading: The Roster-Value Ledger
paragraphs: Value change: -103 points (Indianapolis Colts, Nov 21–Nov 23).
Indianapolis Colts: 55,961 to 55,858 (103 lower). The 100.8 total reflects 20.7 from leading starter Ladd McConkey.

sections.heading: The Evidence in Their Favor
paragraphs: Ladd gave rivals a big number and no final score to hide behind.
An earned mention goes to Ladd McConkey: 20.7. Previous outing: 12.6 (Week 8). On-field production: 5/8 rec, 37 yds, 2 TD.

sections.heading: The Crowd Is Already Too Loud
paragraphs: The crowd discussed Ladd McConkey's 20.7-point return. The irritating part: Ladd McConkey came through with 20.7 fantasy points for Indianapolis Colts. Compliments are free, but the number is earned.
The rest of the debate starts with Chase Brown at 8.6. Arizona Cardinals are unlikely to hand out partial credit for good intentions.

Indianapolis Colts put up 100.8 against Tennessee Titans, while Chase Brown registered 8.6. In the scoreboard interrogation, that is a conspicuous number; the argument gets weaker every time the score is read aloud.

sections.heading: Week 12 Gets the Same Weak Spot First
paragraphs: Arizona Cardinals are waiting in Week 12 at 7-4 and No. 9 overall. After 100.8 points against Tennessee Titans, Indianapolis Colts must show its scoring is repeatable against Arizona Cardinals.
The AFC SOUTH standings list Indianapolis Colts at No. 23. Their 100.8-point performance against Tennessee Titans is evidence for the next race discussion, not a guaranteed berth.
The win puts Indianapolis Colts at 4-7 before Arizona Cardinals. The next lineup needs more from Chase Brown after an 8.6-point Week 11; Arizona Cardinals get to test whether that slot improves.

inquirer_article.byline: By Nick Swindell, Senior Football Correspondent

sections.heading: What Week 11 Changed
paragraphs: Jacksonville Jags did not need a miracle to beat Houston Texans; it needed more ordinary production in too many ordinary places.
A week earlier, Jacksonville Jags lost to New York Jets 37.7–107.2; that Week 10 result belongs in the comparison, but the current Sunday gets its own evaluation.
What Sunday exposed: The Jags got something from Calvin Ridley, but the starters behind him did not produce enough to reach Houston Texans’ total.

sections.heading: Who Actually Moved the Game
paragraphs: Against Houston Texans, Calvin Ridley led the Jags with 17.8 fantasy points; 5 receptions on 6 targets for 68 yards and 1 receiving touchdown.
Calvin Ridley carried a large share while Noah Fant supplied 3.9. The staff must decide whether that gap leaves the lineup too dependent on one starter.

sections.heading: Credit Where It Is Due
paragraphs: The veteran receiver gave Jacksonville Jags a performance good enough to deserve a better result; the loss belongs farther down the lineup card. Calvin Ridley changed from 0.0 in Week 10 to 17.8 in Week 11; the lead score put a brighter number on this Sunday.

sections.heading: The Decisions That Survived Sunday
paragraphs: Cam Ward scored 20.6 more than Justin Fields from the bench while super flex was occupied. That hurts.

paragraphs: Week 11 changed the number for Justin Fields without changing the problem. -0.3 points is still a quiet lineup spot.

reporter.title: Columnist at Large
reporter.voice: Overeducated, theatrical hometown columnist and shameless fan. Longer flowing sentences, cultured and self-aware pretension, elegant insults, dramatic sighs, literary wit and polished sarcasm. He is witty and emotional, never the boring analytics desk, and treats players and managers like characters in an ongoing social comedy while keeping the imagery football-first instead of leaning on a recurring house motif.

inquirer_article.headline: Tennessee Titans Spill Week 11 All Over the Scoreboard
inquirer_article.byline: By Bartholomew Roycington III, Columnist at Large
inquirer_article.deck: The Velvet Rope • Week 11 • Regular Season

sections.heading: This Sunday, Properly Dressed
paragraphs: The Titans got exposed in enough places that Week 12 does not need a mystery—just a toolbox. Tennessee Titans lost to Indianapolis Colts 72.3–100.8, leaving the Titans at 7-4 and No. 11 in the league standings.
A 28.5-point loss means Tennessee Titans needed help in several lineup spots; Josh Hines-Allen alone was nowhere near enough to match Indianapolis Colts.
The Titans went from one good storyline to one bad one.

sections.heading: The Problem Everybody Can See
paragraphs: DK Metcalf fell from 15.4 in Week 10 to 1.2 in Week 11. The 14.2-point reduction leaves Tennessee Titans looking for a measurable correction from DK Metcalf next Sunday.

sections.heading: Week 11: The Part Everybody Will Quote
paragraphs: Denver Doncos earned a headline against Los Angeles Chargers; the final margin gives the rivals something measurable to argue about. Forget the preamble: Denver Doncos beat Los Angeles Chargers 93.4–78.2, leaving the Doncos at 11-0 and No. 1 in the league standings.
Denver Doncos have a recent win to frame, but Javonte Williams cannot sing every part of the next one.

sections.heading: Somebody Own the Bad Part
paragraphs: Jacob Martin posted 3.5 for the Doncos; 3 solo, 1 assist; winning keeps the siren off, but somebody still needs to check that outlet.
The starting return: Jacob Martin at 3.5. Prior recorded return: 17.6.

sections.heading: Who Made the Noise
paragraphs: Against Los Angeles Chargers, Javonte Williams led the Doncos with 24.1 fantasy points; rushing and receiving: 18 carries, 67 rush yds, 1 rush TD, 3/3 rec, 24 rec yds, 1 rec TD.
George Pickens recorded 1 carry for 6 yards, 7 catches on 10 targets for 102 yards, 1 receiving touchdown.
George Pickens had 43.5 last Sunday and 23.8 now.

sections.heading: Management Has to Wear This One
paragraphs: Kimani Vidal beat Emeka Egbuka by 3.6.
Jakeslomiak21 made the roster headline concrete: added Israel Abanikanda and dropped Lan Larison. Its 15.2-point winning spread remains intact in the alternate calculation.

sections.heading: The Name That Earned the Headline
paragraphs: The high-end back supplied the big number and got a win instead of a sympathy card. Javonte Williams had 7.7 last Sunday and 24.1 now. Somebody in the rival chat just retired last week's joke.

sections.heading: The Roster-Value Ledger
paragraphs: Denver Doncos finished Nov 21–Nov 23 with -59 points of recorded value movement.
Denver Doncos: 61,872 to 61,813 (59 lower). Individual leader: Javonte Williams at 24.1; recorded opponent: Los Angeles Chargers.

sections.heading: The Crowd Has Decided, Temporarily
paragraphs: The Doncos fan orchestra has a new conductor: Javonte Williams and 24.1 points. The rest of the musicians are being asked to rehearse after Jacob Martin played a 3.5-point solo nobody ordered.
Supporters will tolerate one rehearsal disaster. A second one against Carolina Panthers get reviewed by the entire neighborhood.

reporter.title: Tabloid Sports Editor
reporter.voice: Hometown tabloid lifer and unapologetic fan. Shorter punchy paragraphs, banner-headline rhythm, loud jokes, shameless celebration after wins, merciless annoyance after dumb losses, and a constant instinct for the sentence rival managers will screenshot. He does not use capitalization for emphasis; the punch comes from wording, rhythm and sarcasm rather than shouting typography.
reporter.signature: If it happened, it belongs in 48-point type.

inquirer_article.headline: Chicago Bears Made Week 11 Ugly
inquirer_article.byline: By Tilly Fleecer, Tabloid Sports Editor
inquirer_article.deck: The Back Page • Week 11 • Regular Season

sections.heading: Week 11: The Part Everybody Will Quote
paragraphs: The Bears got exposed in enough places that Week 12 does not need a mystery—just a toolbox.
The Bears have two recent losses. Dak Prescott needs more help across the lineup.

sections.heading: Who Made the Noise
paragraphs: Against Detroit Lions, Dak Prescott led the Bears with 35.4 fantasy points; passing: 28/33 passing, 325 pass yds, 4 pass TD, 4 carries, 9 rush yds, 1 rush TD.

sections.heading: Management Has to Wear This One
paragraphs: Braelon Allen's 5.1-point edge over Chris Godwin Jr. makes that flex choice sting. Chicago Bears have 5.1 points from Braelon Allen to account for before choosing the next flex starter.

sections.heading: Somebody Own the Bad Part
paragraphs: Chris Godwin Jr. handed Chicago Bears 4.3 points; 3/3 rec, 13 yds; one normal contribution there would have made Monday much quieter.
The starting return: Chris Godwin Jr. at 4.3. Prior recorded return: 4.8.

sections.heading: The Name That Earned the Headline
paragraphs: The high-end quarterback brought the fireworks; too many teammates showed up holding wet matches.
The scorebook credits Dak Prescott with 35.4. Prior recorded return: 32.1. On-field production: 28/33 passing • 325 pass yds • 4 pass TD • 4 carries, 9 rush yds, 1 rush TD.

sections.heading: The Roster-Value Ledger
paragraphs: Chicago Bears finished Nov 21–Nov 23 with +305 points of recorded value movement. Roster value: 47,942 before, 48,247 after.
Chicago Bears rose from 47,942 to 48,247 valuation points. Its 96.5-point Sunday against Detroit Lions was a separate contest.

sections.heading: The Crowd Has Decided, Temporarily
paragraphs: Fans spent Monday treating Chicago Bears’ result like a family wedding: the speeches were awkward and somebody blamed the seating arrangement. 96.5 points against Detroit Lions are the one detail nobody can edit out of the photographs.
The useful conversation starts with Dak Prescott scoring 35.4 and ends with what has to change before New York Jets. Everything between is catering criticism.
Put Chris Godwin Jr. at 4.3 beside Chicago Bears at 96.5 in the fashion column. The Detroit Lions matchup supplies the context; another press conference will not recover the points.

sections.heading: Week 12: No Hiding Now
paragraphs: Forget the preamble: Chicago Bears get New York Jets in Week 12, and New York Jets bring a 5-6 record plus No. 19 overall.
The Bears are not alone in a crowded NFC NORTH race. Within NFC NORTH, the immediate competition is Minnesota Vikings (8-3), Detroit Lions (8-3), and Green Bay Packers (4-7). No one gets a free pass.
Week 12 puts the Bears opposite a New York Jets roster that just got 27.7 from Nakobe Dean, making that production the first matchup problem the Bears lineup has to answer.
The Bears got exposed in enough places that Week 12 does not need a mystery—just a toolbox.
The Bears have two recent losses. Dak Prescott needs more help across the lineup.
Against Detroit Lions, Dak Prescott led the Bears with 35.4 fantasy points; passing: 28/33 passing, 325 pass yds, 4 pass TD, 4 carries, 9 rush yds, 1 rush TD.
Braelon Allen's 5.1-point edge over Chris Godwin Jr. makes that flex choice sting. Chicago Bears have 5.1 points from Braelon Allen to account for before choosing the next flex starter.
Chris Godwin Jr. handed Chicago Bears 4.3 points; 3/3 rec, 13 yds; one normal contribution there would have made Monday much quieter.
The starting return: Chris Godwin Jr. at 4.3. Prior recorded return: 4.8.
The high-end quarterback brought the fireworks; too many teammates showed up holding wet matches.
The scorebook credits Dak Prescott with 35.4. Prior recorded return: 32.1. On-field production: 28/33 passing • 325 pass yds • 4 pass TD • 4 carries, 9 rush yds, 1 rush TD.
Chicago Bears finished Nov 21–Nov 23 with +305 points of recorded value movement. Roster value: 47,942 before, 48,247 after.
Chicago Bears rose from 47,942 to 48,247 valuation points. Its 96.5-point Sunday against Detroit Lions was a separate contest.

Fans spent Monday treating Chicago Bears’ result like a family wedding: the speeches were awkward and somebody blamed the seating arrangement. 96.5 points against Detroit Lions are the one detail nobody can edit out of the photographs.
The useful conversation starts with Dak Prescott scoring 35.4 and ends with what has to change before New York Jets. Everything between is catering criticism.
Put Chris Godwin Jr. at 4.3 beside Chicago Bears at 96.5 in the fashion column. The Detroit Lions matchup supplies the context; another press conference will not recover the points.

inquirer_article.headline: Detroit Lions Scored Enough to Make Chicago Bears’ Total Irrelevant
inquirer_article.byline: By Jefferson Filch, Investigations & Front Office
inquirer_article.deck: The Inquiry Desk • Week 11 • Regular Season

sections.heading: Week 11 Was Not Subtle
paragraphs: Week 11 made the Lions considerably harder to dismiss than anyone waiting on a quick collapse had planned. The irritating part: Detroit Lions beat Chicago Bears 98.4–96.5, leaving the Lions at 8-3 and No. 7 in the league standings.
Emmett Johnson earned the Lions headline; Parker Washington supplied the part that made Chicago Bears reachable.

sections.heading: Fix It Before It Becomes a Bit
paragraphs: Matt Hibner beat Michael Mayer by 1.8.

TomKatz changed the Week 11 roster: dropped Demarcus Robinson; acquired Tykee Smith by trade; added Nohl Williams and dropped Byron Murphy Jr. Nohl Williams made the starting lineup immediately and scored 17.5 points.

sections.heading: The Names Rivals Have to Respect
paragraphs: Against Chicago Bears, Emmett Johnson led the Lions with 24.3 fantasy points; rushing and receiving: 23 carries, 105 rush yds, 1 rush TD, 4/4 rec, 38 rec yds.

sections.heading: The Thing Everybody Saw
paragraphs: Detroit Lions got its softest Week 11 number from Michael Mayer at 1.4; 1/4 rec, 4 yds; the standings point prevents a full roast.
Michael Mayer: 1.4 for Detroit Lions. Previous outing: 3.8 (Week 10).

sections.heading: The Roster-Value Ledger
paragraphs: Measured roster value moved -68 points for Detroit Lions during the November 21–November 23 valuation window. Roster value: 54,469 before, 54,401 after.
From 54,469 to 54,401: that was Detroit Lions' market move. Chicago Bears saw 98.4 fantasy points on the actual board.

sections.heading: The Evidence in Their Favor
paragraphs: The high-end back put up the number that forces rivals to argue about somebody else.
Credit Emmett Johnson for 24.3. Previous outing: 35.1 (Week 10). On-field production: 23 carries, 105 rush yds, 1 rush TD • 4/4 rec, 38 rec yds.

sections.heading: The Crowd Is Already Too Loud
paragraphs: The fan base weighed Emmett Johnson's 24.3-point return. Against Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions earned the scoreboard figure 98.4. Calling it destiny would be a terrible use of a calculator.
File that under obvious: Emmett Johnson and Michael Mayer were separated by real production; Buffalo Billiards get a chance to discover whether the manager noticed.
Michael Mayer produced 1.4 for Detroit Lions in the Chicago Bears matchup. The 98.4-point team total makes it a rather awkward figure; the scorekeeper has exhausted the sympathy budget.

sections.heading: Week 12 Gets the Same Weak Spot First
paragraphs: Detroit Lions meet Buffalo Billiards next, and Buffalo Billiards enter at 0-11 (No. 32 overall).

sections.heading: What Week 11 Changed
paragraphs: Green Bay Packers have useful pieces, but Week 11 showed how quickly a few quiet slots can turn those pieces into wasted decoration. Green Bay Packers lost to Minnesota Vikings 53.3–113.0, leaving the Packers at 4-7 and No. 26 in the league standings.
Green Bay Packers came out of Week 10 with a 54.2–74.8 loss to Arizona Cardinals; That 53.3-point Sunday must be judged alongside the previous result, not mistaken for the whole season.

sections.heading: Who Actually Moved the Game
paragraphs: Against Minnesota Vikings, Travis Kelce led the Packers with 25.4 fantasy points; 6 receptions on 7 targets for 74 yards and 2 receiving touchdowns.
Saquon Barkley recorded 17 carries for 75 yards, 1 rushing touchdown.

sections.heading: Credit Where It Is Due
paragraphs: The high-end tight end set a winning level for Green Bay Packers even though the final result refused to cooperate. After a 5.0-point Week 10, the lead score reached 25.4 and turned Week 11 into the louder of the two.

sections.heading: This Sunday, Properly Dressed
paragraphs: Minnesota Vikings beat Green Bay Packers 113.0–53.3, leaving the Vikings at 8-3 and No. 4 in the league standings.
Two wins have the Vikings making noise for a reason.

sections.heading: The People Who Made the Afternoon Interesting
paragraphs: Against Green Bay Packers, Will Anderson Jr. led the Vikings with 28.7 fantasy points; defensive: 2 solo, 3 assists, 1 sack, 2 TFL, 4 QB hits.

sections.heading: The Credit Ledger, With Reservations
paragraphs: The high-end lineman brought the fireworks and the rest of the lineup remembered to light something too. After a 23.4-point Week 10, the headliner reached 28.7 and gave Week 11 the stronger jolt.

sections.heading: Management, Vanity and the Cost of Choices
paragraphs: Jgeiss22 hit the Week 11 wire and added Josh Johnson and dropped David Njoku; added David Njoku and dropped DeMarvion Overshown. Management put Josh Johnson straight into the Week 11 starting card, where he scored 8.8 points.
Management has one loud question before New England Patriots: Darren Waller in the current starting spot. The correction has to appear in the lineup before it shows up in Monday’s excuses.

sections.heading: Week 11: The Part Everybody Will Quote
paragraphs: Atlanta Falcons defeated Carolina Panthers with contributions from Quinnen Williams and Austin Booker.
Two wins have the Falcons making noise for a reason.

sections.heading: Somebody Own the Bad Part
paragraphs: 1.4 points from Elijah Higgins left the Falcons asking for more; 1/1 rec, 4 yds; fine—ask politely while holding the win.
The weak return belonged to Elijah Higgins: 1.4. Prior recorded return: 3.1.

sections.heading: Who Made the Noise
paragraphs: The Atlanta Falcons box against Carolina Panthers put Quinnen Williams on 43.0 fantasy points, followed by Austin Booker on 25.0. That pair accounts for a clear share of the 112.4-point finish.
Against Carolina Panthers, Quinnen Williams led the Falcons with 43.0 fantasy points; defensive: 4 solo, 1 assist, 2 sacks, 3 TFL, 3 QB hits.

sections.heading: Management Has to Wear This One
paragraphs: The missed SUPER FLEX call: Chimere Dike beat Elijah Higgins by 11.9. The win margin measured 55.5; the recorded reserve advantage was 11.9.

sections.heading: The Roster-Value Ledger
paragraphs: Between the two market observations, Atlanta Falcons recorded a +221-point difference in roster value. Recorded values: 38,835 before, 39,056 now.

sections.heading: The Crowd Has Decided, Temporarily
paragraphs: The radio station covering Atlanta Falcons has declared its phone lines a public utility after that 112.4-point showing. The callers are competing to invent the grandest compliment. Quinnen Williams at 43.0 remains the one indisputable contribution.
The station can turn the volume down for Los Angeles Chargers. The lineup cannot afford to.

reporter.voice: Old-school hometown beat writer, lifelong fan and practiced pessimist. Clipped declarative paragraphs, deep institutional memory, dry sarcasm, grudging praise, real affection for the team, and a habit of connecting this Sunday to the season that came before it. sections.heading: What Week 11 Changed
paragraphs: The Aints have a clean Week 12 assignment now: keep the parts that worked and stop subsidizing the ones that did not. New Orleans Aints lost to Tampa Bay Buccaneers 77.2–116.8, leaving the Aints at 9-2 and No. 3 in the league standings.
New Orleans Aints have both a winning and losing recent example. Chuba Hubbard can help decide which version survives next.

paragraphs: The quiet end of New Orleans Aints belonged to J.K. Dobbins at 0.0; 1 carry, 0 rush yds; a near-empty line like that is a roster question, not background scenery.

sections.heading: Week 11 Was Not Subtle
paragraphs: The irritating part: Los Angeles Rams lost to San Francisco 49ers 104.0–105.4, leaving the Rams at 5-6 and No. 17 in the league standings.
Los Angeles Rams got a usable top score from George Karlaftis, but San Francisco 49ers finished with more total production across the matchup.
The Rams have lost their last two games.

sections.heading: The Names Rivals Have to Respect
paragraphs: File that under obvious: Against San Francisco 49ers, George Karlaftis led the Rams with 42.3 fantasy points; defensive: 3 solo, 1 assist, 2.5 sacks, 2 TFL, 5 QB hits.
James Cook III recorded 22 carries for 89 yards, 1 rushing touchdown, 2 catches on 2 targets for 3 yards.

sections.heading: Fix It Before It Becomes a Bit
paragraphs: T.J. Watt kept the IDP flex job while Jacob Rodriguez scored 20.6 extra points from the bench. T.J. Watt started in the IDP FLEX slot. Jacob Rodriguez beat that choice by 20.6.

sections.heading: The Thing Everybody Saw
paragraphs: Jaylen Wright gave Los Angeles Rams 1.0 this week after 3.5 in Week 10. That is the same problem twice, not progress.

sections.heading: What Week 11 Changed
paragraphs: David Bailey gave San Francisco 49ers the performance it needed, and the rest of the lineup supplied enough answers to make it count. San Francisco 49ers beat Los Angeles Rams 105.4–104.0, leaving the 49ers at 8-3 and No. 6 in the league standings.
San Francisco 49ers split the last two Sundays by responding to Week 10. The win matters most as proof that the first result did not have to repeat.
David Bailey led the 49ers scoring, while the rest of the lineup supplied enough points to keep the result from depending on one name.

sections.heading: Who Actually Moved the Game
paragraphs: Against Los Angeles Rams, David Bailey led the 49ers with 37.4 fantasy points; defensive: 2 solo, 3 assists, 2 sacks, 2 TFL, 2 QB hits.
Ashton Jeanty recorded 11 carries for 79 yards, 5 catches on 8 targets for 90 yards, 1 receiving touchdown.
Jeanty turned the top of the lineup into a two-player problem for Los Angeles Rams. Ashton Jeanty had 10.4 last Sunday and 27.9 now. That second scorer shift scored more than in Week 10.

sections.heading: The Decisions That Survived Sunday
paragraphs: Reserve Marlin Klein finished 8.1 ahead of Luther Burden III despite the latter occupying flex. The scorecard lists a 1.4-point win and an unused 8.1-point edge.

sections.heading: The Problem That Cannot Follow Them Into Week 12
paragraphs: Week 10 gave Chase Young more than Week 11 did. After 4.0 this time, the 49ers should treat the role as a Week 12 question, not a coincidence.
Shortfall: Chase Young returned 4.0. Previous week on record: 5.5.

sections.heading: Credit Where It Is Due
paragraphs: The high-end linebacker supplied the anchor and let San Francisco 49ers play normal football around it. David Bailey had 12.5 last Sunday and 37.4 now. That was an increase from Week 10.

sections.heading: The Roster-Value Ledger
paragraphs: The Nov 21–Nov 23 value sheet records +61 points for San Francisco 49ers.

paragraphs: The neighborhood watch has politely declined jurisdiction over San Francisco 49ers’ starting decisions. David Bailey's 37.4 points are evidence of what worked, while the rest of the scoreboard is a less convincing witness.
Fans are not asking for a criminal inquiry. They are asking the next lineup to look like somebody reviewed the last one.
